title: Coherent Errors: Chess Transformers Act on Misremembered Boards
content: Long-horizon failure is reported as one number, which confounds two failures with opposite remedies: the model has lost track of the world, or it holds the world and chooses badly. We separate them where an exact state oracle exists, chess from move notation with no search at inference, in models of 3,440,064 to 39,884,288 parameters, reading linear probes against the true position at every token. Aggregate state fidelity, the quantity usually reported, is the weaker predictor of an illegal next move within a fixed depth, at AUC 0.538 to 0.671 against 0.592 to 0.687 for the same representation restricted to the squares the move touches. And the errors are coherent. Reconstructing the position the model appears to believe, 0.355 of its illegal moves are legal there, against 0.050 for the same move under another position’s belief and 0.007 for an arbitrary illegal move. Editing the probe direction encoding an occupied square removes 0.934 of the probability mass on moves from it, a norm-matched random edit 0.077, so the representation is read and not merely present. Belief consistency rises monotonically across six model sizes, though the causal edit is not measured at every size. A substantial identified subset of long-horizon error is coherent with a degraded state the policy demonstrably reads. We report failures too: a backwards layer profile, a degenerate pre-registered metric, an auxiliary objective improving the measurement of state more than its consequences, and a second domain needing seven designs to become measurable.
